title: Book 14 opens: churchgoers must be washed of sin’s stain
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK FOURTEEN. That those willing to frequent in churches must be clean and washed-out as to the stain from sin, and thus stand beside God.

Cyril: So then concerning the tent and indeed also concerning priests and Levitical under-service these things seem to me to have been said most sufficiently, and I think to have been examined finely. Fit
translator_notes: Ends mid Πρέ into §2 ποι; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Ascend Lord’s house clean; eject leper/flux/soul-unclean from camp
english: Cyril: …ting would be most of all for those who would choose to live rightly, and the altogether well-fitting of the citizenship in Christ, as a kind of crown to bind upon their own heads, to urge one another headlong as it were saying: ‘Come, and let us go up unto the mountain of Lord, and unto the house of the God of Jacob, and he will announce to us his way, and we will walk in it;’ when also some having received the thus well-famed and benefit-bearing voice, all but also leap up saying: ‘I was gladdened upon those having said to me: Unto a house of Lord we will go.’ So then, O Palladius, for those hastening to go unto a house of God, of what sort would the aim be and the mind for them wherever then it would look, and what longing to set upright, they go unto the sacred and divine tent?
Palladius: And indeed, O companion, the matter is not unclear; for it has been written, that ‘Worship the Lord in his holy court;’ and ‘Lift sacrifices, and go into his courts.’

Cyril: So then bringing forward the sacrifices over themselves, clear that the spiritual ones, and indeed also about to approach according to intelligible worship, some go into the house of Lord and into his courts.
Palladius: Thus I say.

Cyril: So then shall we think those willing to frequent-in, must dart through simply, not having been washed-out as to the sin, not having been freed from abomination, not having been scraped-off as it were of the filth of flesh-love, but having the mind melted-in, and having a rusted heart? Least at least, but rather having been brightened with the brightness in Christ, and gleaming-through the all-variegated beauty of the most God-loving virtue.
Palladius: Very much so; for I at least say one must go according to eyes of Lord, with every stain of our thoughts having been rubbed-out beforehand.

Cyril: You spoke rightly, since at least he also makes the sick one hated, and indeed also rejectable, and sends out from the multitude of the holy ones. Which also the all-divine Paul writing understands very well: ‘So then lift out the evil one from yourselves.’ And I would not say the matter a fruit of wildness of customs, but a wise finding of safety. ‘For a little leaven,’ he says, ‘leavens the whole lump.’ This again also a sacred law was under-forming for us riddlingly. For it has been written in the Numbers: ‘And the Lord spoke toward Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them send out from the camp every leper and every flux-flowing, and every unclean upon soul, from male unto female, send out outside the camp, and they will not defile their camps in which I lodge in them. And the sons of Israel did thus.’ So then is it not true to say that very hard-to-bear and truly hard-to-carry is the burden of the law? For you understand how also upon unwilling sicknesses he writes-down a judgment, and yet
translator_notes: Ends mid καίτοι into §3 κατοικτείρεσθαι; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Bodily ills type spiritual; leper = flesh works; flux begins
english: Cyril: …one must pity those having fallen into such misfortunes; for in return for what then would someone puzzle also very reasonably, that he was making the leper houseless and sendable-away, and indeed toward these also the one held-down by a passion of flux-flow, and again the unclean upon soul?
Palladius: I would not have to understand, and you yourself would perhaps speak.

Cyril: So then I think that of the things in thickness and bodily matters there was not a very great word beside God, for the one pre-forming for us the divine and spiritual worship. For the things outside law are punished, and as many as appear having stepped out of the fitting, these I would say are under judgment and justice, but a bodily sickness would in no manner strike against the laws. So then it will lie reasonably also farthest from a writing, and the being charged toward someone it would not have from anywhere; or is it not clear for everyone, that no one is sick willingly, and everyone then, I think, makes being well-strong most wishable?
Palladius: Truly.

Cyril: So then even if the word should have something unbeautiful of the history, the grieving is nothing, if the spiritual things should be led through well toward at least what seems good to the lawgiver. So then leprosy is a dying of flesh, and the passion most devouring. Therefore also the all-divine Moses, with Miriam having been leproused for him, having become fearful, and very cheerless, was entreating, saying: ‘O God, I beg you, heal her,’ for he said: ‘Let her not become as a miscarriage going out from a mother’s womb, and it will eat down the half of her fleshes.’ And a flux-flowing, what would I say, of what sort the passion? for no one has been ignorant. And at least that some are unclean upon soul, signals some such thing: the touching a departed one and becoming near a dead body, the law was reckoning for the more ancient ones unto a manner of defilement, showing the deadness hated to God the one able to make-alive all things. And indeed also otherwise, receiving the matter unto a dying of mind and soul as in a thick type. And a dead and cooled-out mind, the sin-loving, and accustomed to be without-share of the manly-acts unto life. But if it happened for some to have died, somehow every necessity, for those own from blood and according to race to understand and to do upon him the things having been customed; yet unclean also these according to the law, and not altogether and unto all, but there was for them some manner of cleansing-back. You have a sufficient clarifying of the history.
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: So then come, transforming it unto spiritual contemplation, let us say that: that the leper signals for us the one having been spotted with varied passions unto youthfulness. And these are the works of the flesh, which also the most wise Paul himself was numbering for us saying: ‘Fornication, uncleanness, idolatry, enmities, strife, angers, jealousies.’ And another at least,
translator_notes: Ends mid Ἕτερός γε μὴν into §4 τοῦτ' ἔστιν ὁ γονοῤῥυής; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Flux = wasted fertility; soul-unclean = share others’ deadness; crushed/cut begin
english: Cyril: …that is, the flux-flowing, the one always and unrestrainedly in defilements, and spending the fitness of the nature toward virtuous and admirable fruit-bearing unto nothing.
Palladius: And of what sort do you say?

Cyril: Broad very much is the word upon all; and for now I will use one clear and most vivid example, toward proof of what I said: those having a well-natured mind and as it were somehow scraped-off, putting it into the words about the truth, will they not have the well-fitting in rightness and exactness of doctrines as a fruit not unadmirable?
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: And those at least having chosen not to think and do this, but rather turning aside from the necessary way, and setting up an advocate of unholy doctrines, or showing a helper of the wickedness in world, make a begetter of deceit and deception, damaging for nothing useful the fitness of the nature toward the good, and they write-down for us very well the flux-flowing, and show a soul-weakness same-natured with a bodily passion in own manners.
Palladius: You spoke rightly.

Cyril: And the unclean upon soul somehow altogether signals the one having shared of others’ deadness, and being filled lazily with alien faults, toward whom also the divine David somehow said: ‘If you were seeing a thief, you were running-with him, and with an adulterer you were setting your portion.’ For just as doing what is not lawful damages and deadens soul and mind, so also consenting with those doing them, and the one willing-with would also be a sharer with those self-working unto sin. For he is not somehow unchargeable. Therefore also Paul: ‘Keep yourself pure,’ he says, ‘and do not share alien sins;’ this, I think, is the being defiled upon a dead one intelligibly.
Palladius: It seems so.

Cyril: So then he has ordered very well the leper and flux-flowing and unclean upon the soul to depart from the synagogue, not allowing those having the hard-to-wash-out uncleanness to be woven-up with the choruses of the holy ones? ‘For what sharing of light toward darkness? or what portion for a faithful with an unfaithful?’ he says.
Palladius: So then slippery, the going as with unwashed feet into a house of God.

Cyril: Most slippery indeed, if at least it is true that striking against God is not without-damage. And he also shuts out others from the holy court in Deuteronomy, saying: ‘A crushed one and a cut-off one will not go into a church of Lord, one from a whore will not go into a church of Lord; an Ammonite and a Moabite will not go into a church of Lord, and unto a tenth generation will not go into a church of Lord, and unto the age, because of the not’
translator_notes: Ends mid παρὰ τὸ μὴ into §5 συναντῆσαι; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Crushed vs cut manhood type; Ammon=heretics; Moab=idolaters
english: Cyril: …meeting them for you with breads and water in the way, with you going out from Egypt, and that they hired against you Balaam son of Beor from Mesopotamia to curse you. And Lord your God did not wish to hearken to Balaam, and Lord your God turned the curses into a blessing, because Lord your God loved you. You will not address peaceful things to them, and beneficial things for them, all your days unto the age.’
Palladius: And who would be understood crushed and cut-off, Ammonite and Moabite, I would wish to learn thoroughly.

Cyril: Hear then; the of the making of eunuchs is not one manner, not one, O Palladius, but some double is said to be, and has been found-out. For some are cutters and having been torn-apart as to the male things; and others still bear crushed and altogether useless things, and some sometimes cut-off rawly and unholily the child-making part of the body, and are inactive toward the of a man, and yet finishing among men by nature and age; and a symbol of manliness, the male things. So then one must suspect the crushed, the as it were somehow not having been pulled-out altogether as to soul and mind, but rather somehow saving in himself the shattered manliness upon goods, and indeed the cut-off, the one having thrown them away wholly, and having been deprived of the things most fitting for men. And in equal as it were a charge, with the not wishing to man-up at all, the loving not to man-up healthily.
Palladius: Of what sort then do you say?

Cyril: Some have fallen-back into fleshly desires, having released as it were whole reins to the passion, throwing-beside the mind rotten and unmanly to the pleasures unto wantonness. And others again wonder at continence, and sometimes touch the bright attempts unto this, but fear-out the standing-against, and not bearing the assault of the pleasure, they nod-down toward the strengthless. So then, will you not reasonably call the one having altogether given-up the attempts unto manliness cut-off? And the one having in mind the wishing to man-up, yet not still also being strong to set upright the virtue, will you think crushed, reshaping urbanely also the passions of the body unto a quality of manners, and receiving the in sense as an image of the intelligible and more unapparent?
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: And with these was being shut-out-together both Ammonite and Moabite, as unholy and most abominable, and springing-upon the holy ones as lions, and pouring upon those accustomed to be well-reputed the arrows from envy and malice. And they would be a type, Ammonites at least, of the unpitiful heretics. And Moabites again, of those still in the idolatrous wanderings, and having been underlaid with the wickednesses of the demons; for both God-hated, and as it were sick with a brother boldness against the holy ones.

title: Ammon/Edom refuse bread; heretics kin who will not help
english: Palladius: I do not very much understand what you say.

Cyril: You understand very well, and not unto long. For Ammonites having become of Esau, were near-sown and same-blooded to the sons from Jacob, I say to Israel; but also somehow neglecting the nature itself, those from Esau were falsifying the manner of kinship, and fearful and unbending were thereafter bearing-down toward those near and from blood, that is of the Israel. For when departing from the of Egyptians he was running-past the land of the Ammonites, he was entreating the dweller as a brother to let-pass, or for them to dart-through and to pity those having been wronged; and he was not releasing. And what do I say this? Rather even in arms, or also he lifts a war. And he would have wronged terribly, if not according to a divine voice, Israel has bent-away; and the having-been-written holds thus: ‘And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh toward a king of Edom, saying: Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the labor having found us. And our fathers went down into Egypt, and we sojourned in Egypt more days, and the Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers. And we cried up toward Lord, and Lord hearkened to our voice, and having sent messengers, led us out from Egypt. And now we are in Kadesh city, from a part of your borders. We will go past through your land. We will not go through through fields, nor through vineyards, nor will we drink water from your pits. By a royal way we will walk; we will not turn aside right nor left, until we should go past your borders. And Edom said toward him: You will not go through through me. And if not, in war I will go out unto a meeting for you.’ And after other things: ‘And Edom went out unto a meeting for him in a heavy crowd, and in a strong hand. And Edom did not wish to give to Israel to go past through his borders. And Israel turned aside from him.’ So then is the word thereafter not clear and vivid?
Palladius: Not somehow very much.

Cyril: For you do not understand that having been joined to those from Israel by a relation according to near-kinship, unloving and hard, and having differed nothing from wild beasts, they were being convicted from the matters themselves? For needing to pity as brothers, being in sweats and labors, they go out having devastated. Therefore the law says: ‘They will not go into a church of Lord, because of their not meeting you with bread and water, with you going out from Egypt,’ that is, through the very unsympathetic, and having gone out from wild ones unto unholiness of manners. And you may see that such toward us the ones having chosen to walk-straight are the peoples and leaders of the heretics. For as far as it came unto at least knowing one and only God the Father, and accepting the faith unto Son and the Spirit, even if they do not have altogether healthily an untrue opinion of the brotherhood toward us, and they bear-bastard the kin by judgment, yet for those being in persecutions they do not help, but rather also
translator_notes: Ends mid μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ into §7 ταῖς παρὰ σφῶν; PG mid-cut kept. Cyril conflates Ammon/Edom in typology—render Greek as written.

title: Heretic workshops like Ammon; Moab=Hellenes; no greeting
english: Cyril: …they load-on with the wickednesses from themselves. ‘For from us they went out, but they were not from us,’ according to the having-been-written. ‘For if they were from us, they would have remained with us.’ To whom also the Savior himself, having the fairness plastered-on, yet not still also accustomed to do the things unto his glory, would address also very reasonably: ‘The one not being with me, is against me, and the one not gathering with me, scatters.’ So then do the God-hated workshops of the heretics seem to you to resemble Ammonites, having been sickly extraordinarily as to the unsympathetic and un-God-loving?
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: And observe also Moabites, if it seems good, being most warlike openly for those willing to serve God the only both by nature and truly. For they were worshipers of idols, having taken heart exceptionally in divinations and sorceries, and having been fluttered not moderately about flights of birds, and grinding the teeth at the good-doings of Israel, they were hiring Balaam, and preparing him to curse, and by the unspeakable power of God, the mouth of the diviner was being reshaped toward blessings unwilling for them. Such would be the war of Hellenes against us, begrudging the glory of our Savior, and raising-up against us every strength of the devil, which the divine and from-above grace shakes-down, pouring the strengthless of the herd of the demons, and setting-up the manner of the plot toward the knowing to gladden.
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: And for Ammonites and indeed also for Moabites, untrodden are the holy things and very reasonably; for for whom the daring things are brother and the boldness same-formed, for these it would be fitting also to spring into the equal-balanced justices. And observe at least the firm of the law; for he removes the holy ones of them altogether, and not even so much as to say he wants to go unto common-speech, he enjoins saying: ‘You will not address peaceful things to them, and beneficial things for them you will not speak, all your days unto the age.’ So then is this not vividly, what also a pair of holy ones has taught us out, both Paul and John? For the one was saying: ‘If someone comes toward you, and does not bear this teaching, do not say rejoice to this one,’ and this, I think, is the, ‘You will not address peaceful things to them, and beneficial things for them.’ And the other again, ‘A heretical human after one and a second admonition, refuse, knowing that such a one has been twisted-out.’ This is the, You will not speak beneficial things for them. For the law says one must yield to those very twisted-out, as to mad ones, saying: ‘Walk by the light of your fire, and by the flame which you kindled.’ But the Ammonite is shut out unto a third generation, and a Moabite even until a tenth, from at least the time, as I think, with God under-showing for us the greatness of the indignation upon both. For lesser, according to the likely, is the justice of heretics; one might say
translator_notes: Ends mid φαίη into §8 γὰρ ἄν τις; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Zeal without knowledge; no covenant with nations; Dinah begins
english: Cyril: …for someone also upon them just as of course also upon the Jews. ‘For I witness for them, that they have a zeal of God, but not according to recognition.’ For thinking to be right-speaking and wise, the wretched ones have escaped themselves, and fighting the doctrines of the truth, and having been overpowered by a molded zeal, they think to speak-with for the glory of God, arraying against those walking-straight. And Moabites at least, that is, the bands of Hellenes, nakedly and openly, and without all holding-back, fight the divine glory. Therefore somehow the law has hung a more burdensome justice for them. Yet both are sendable-away from the sacred enclosures, as profane and God-hated.
Palladius: So then a matter not without-damage, as far as it came unto defilements, the loving to go even at least unto words with some alien and other-minded ones.

Cyril: You understand very well. Therefore also the law walls-off those having been washed-out and clean, and already own to God, from their abomination saying: ‘And it will be in the Lord your God’s leading you into the land into which you go there to inherit it, and you will lift out great and many and strong nations from your face, the Hittite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, seven nations many, and great, and stronger than you, and Lord your God will give them over into your hands, and you will strike them, with an obliteration you will obliterate them. You will not covenant a covenant toward them, nor will you pity them, nor will you marry toward them. Your daughter you will not give to his son, and his daughter you will not take for your son, for he will stand-off your son from me, and he will serve other gods.’ So then firm is the law. ‘For you will not set,’ he says, ‘a covenant toward them;’ for uncombinable and unjoinable for the having-been-sanctified, the still profane, for the having-been-lit, the in mist and dark, for the having-been-received-in the unacceptable; for the one going-in toward a sacred and divine tent, the one being thrust out of this.
Palladius: Then what the forethought of the law? and for the sake of what does it also altogether stand-apart the clean from the profane, even if someone should become in a beauty of the virtue?

Cyril: For very much indeed is the fear, O friend; lest somehow also what seems to have stood rightly should receive-in a shaking upon what is not fitting and be carried-aside from the proper, having been forced somehow by someone, either of a pleasure stirring, or of the inclination being in the nature thrusting-down unto the fault. For somehow it has always bent-away upon the worthless, and a divine word witnesses for us; ‘For carefully lies,’ he says, ‘the mind of the human upon the evil things from youth.’ And I would set beside for you willing unto a vivid proof, as many things as a word says the from Jacob endured.
Palladius: Dinah somehow you say; for I think thus.
Cyril: Very much so, O Palladius; for it has been written thus in the book of the Genesis: ‘And there came’
translator_notes: Ends mid Καὶ ἦλθεν into §9 Ἰακὼβ εἰς Σαλὴμ; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Dinah leaves tent; soul ruined by alien daughters; David’s one ask
english: Cyril: …Jacob unto Salem city of Shechem, which is in land Canaan, when he returned from Mesopotamia of Syria, and he encamped opposite face of the city, and he acquired the portion of the field, where he set there his tent, from Hamor father of Shechem, for a hundred lambs, and he set there an altar, and he called-upon the God of Israel. And Dinah went out, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore for Jacob, to learn thoroughly the daughters of the locals, and Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of the land, saw her. And having taken her, he lay with her. And he humbled her. And he held toward the soul of Dinah the daughter of Jacob. And he loved the virgin, and he spoke according to the mind of the virgin to her.’ So then observe that still loving-to-be and lodging in the tent of the father, in which also he called-upon the God of Israel, and a reverend altar had been raised, she was still unprofane and in the boasts of the virginity. And when she ran out of the paternal tent, and having left the sacred space, was being mixed with alien women, she was being forced at once toward uncustomary profanation, and was no longer a virgin, having been borne under unwillingly at the beginnings by the pleasures of others, and having suffered after this also the wishing to be with the one having overreached. ‘For he spoke,’ he says, ‘according to the mind of the virgin to her.’
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: So then setting beside the sense-perceptible unto an image of the intelligible, come then let us say, that a soul dwelling as it were some exceptional citizenship as a tent, will be all-holy and clean, and having been freed from every abomination, and if it should go out somewhere, and hasten toward the daughters of the alien-tribes, that is, if it should seek-out and spy the life of those in world, the well-natured and well-born mind will be corrupted; for it would not be without-damage for those for whom the aim would become, the living-through brightly, to live-with the worthless. But the divine David at least was not being caught wishing to go outside the sacred tent, but rather to love-to-be and dwell not far, he was making of the things most through prayer saying: ‘One thing I asked from Lord, this I will seek, the dwelling me in a house of Lord all the days of my life, to look-at the delightfulness of Lord, and to visit his holy temple. Because he hid me in his tent in a day of my evils, he sheltered me in a hidden of his tent.’ A tent, I think, saying the divine and sacred, as at least in these, the firm and unshakeable of the pure citizenship, upon which somehow also having gone-in, he was untakeable for those of the passions wishing to devastate.
Palladius: It seems so.

Cyril: And what? would someone not learn more clearly and more truly, that the sharings toward alien-born would somehow produce things beyond every defilement even for those having been trusted to have been fixed, having brought-beside
translator_notes: Ends mid παρενεγκὼν into §10 εἰς ἀπόδειξιν Σολομῶντος; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Solomon’s foreign wives; pleasure dethrones wisdom; no whore in Israel
english: Cyril: …unto a proof the finishing of Solomon’s life, and what things it happened for him to suffer, upon him on a threshold of old-age?
Palladius: How did you speak?

Cyril: For he was thus bright and sung-of, so as somehow already to take the incomparable glory, yet he changed-over unto the unbeautiful, rather even he leaped-down ignobly, unto somehow the last of the impiety unto God. And the things upon him hold thus. For it has been written in the third of the Kingdoms: ‘And Solomon was magnified over all the kings of the earth in wealth and prudence. And all the kings of the earth were seeking the face of Solomon, to hear his prudence, which Lord gave in his heart.’ But the thus well-famed and sung-of, and having driven through unto this of wisdom thereafter, so as to become in unmeasured wonder, and beside those very distinguished, a pleasure of evil women levered-out, and as it were somehow taking him out of the divine tent itself put him into the pits of the idolatry. For it has been written thus about him: ‘And the king Solomon was woman-loving, and he took alien women, and the daughter of Pharaoh; Moabitesses, and Ammonitesses, and Idumaeans, Syrians, Hittites, Amorites, from the nations, which Lord forbade for the sons of Israel: You will not go in toward them, and they themselves will not go in toward you, in order that they may not turn aside your hearts behind their idols. Unto them Solomon was glued, to love. And there were for him ruling women seven hundred, and concubines three hundred. And it became in the time of Solomon’s old-age, and the alien women turned aside his heart behind other gods. And his heart was not complete with Lord his God, just as the heart of David his father. And Solomon walked behind the Astarte abomination of Sidonians, and behind their king idol of sons of Ammon; and Solomon did evil before Lord, and he did not walk behind Lord, as David his father.’ So then is it not worthy to wail for the one said to have suffered such? The one having raised that well-famed temple in the Jerusalems, the one having asked the wisdom sitting-beside the divine thrones, the one having been wondered-at upon the incomparable understanding, and unto the ends themselves of the under heaven, the one as a morning-star, apparent for cities and lands, being worsted by shameful women, and going behind a most polluted pleasure, is caught having fallen unto this of folly, so as also to neglect altogether the piety unto God. So then slippery then and undebatably is the being with the alien-tribes according to the same. And altogether most terrible also the being worsted by the fleshly pleasure, and unclean such a one, and having been hated by the all-holy God, and not without virtue, to drive into the sacred and divine tent. But neither would he bring forward an acceptable sacrifice. For it has been written in Deuteronomy: ‘There will not be a whore from daughters of Israel, and there will not be a whoring one from sons of Israel; and there will not be’
translator_notes: Ends mid καὶ οὐκ ἔσται into later §§; tip §§1–10.
